content.text:
Done. Summary of the work:

## What was wrong
The shipped `weight_decay: 3.0` was tuned on a 4 000-row sample where it wins by collapsing the MLP into an essentially linear model (LDA gets the identical 0.746 on dev). On a calibrated synthetic stand-in for the 80 000-row corpus (Gaussian features matched to the sample, random-MLP teacher, ~20 % uniform crowd noise — consistent with the noise structure I measured on the real data), wd=3 lands at 0.75–0.78 — **below** the 0.805 target — while wd≈0.3 gives 0.87–0.88.

## What I changed in `/app/repo`
- **`train.py`**: new `train_select()` — standardises on the whole corpus, holds out 10 % (seeded by `--seed`), trains one 256-256 MLP per `wd_candidates` entry for `--steps` steps each, ranks them on the noisy hold-out (which I verified ranks models the same way gold labels do at this scale), and predicts with the softmax-average of candidates within 1 pt of the best. A CPU-time guard (`cpu_budget_s`, 95 s) skips remaining candidates if they wouldn't fit. Command line unchanged; output is `int64`, one class per row.
- **`config.json`**: `weight_decay: 0.3`, `wd_candidates: [0.3, 1.0, 0.1, 3.0]` (best-expected first so budget truncation degrades gracefully), plus the selection knobs.
- **`README.md`**: short note on the new behaviour. Repo is 36 KB, code + hyper-parameters only.

## Verification
Full production command on the synthetic 80k corpus, single thread: both seeds select wd=0.3, **test acc 0.867 / 0.8675**, 72 s CPU, 85 MB RSS. Guard path tested with a 1 s budget (stops after the first candidate, still writes valid predictions).

## Report
`/app/report.md` explains the diagnosis, the testbed, the table of results, and what I deliberately didn't do (noise-transition correction, using dev inside the job, bigger models).

Caveat for the team: the 0.87 figure is on the synthetic stand-in; the real teacher function is unknown, but the mechanism now picks regularisation from the actual training data rather than trusting the 5 % sweep.
